prompt:
A full-body vertical 2:3 (1024×1536) character card image of Xu Chu from the Romance of the Three Kingdoms, reimagined as an adult woman — the 'Tiger Fool', Cao Cao's mighty bodyguard who wrestled Ma Chao. Age: mid-twenties — a clear adult face; no facial lines. She is a woman — no beard, moustache or facial hair.

Style (fixed): Korean MMORPG character artwork. A recognisably drawn face with gently simplified anatomical structure. 2D painting with visible brushwork: layered strokes of colour, soft broken edges, thin coloured linework and a few crisp accents on the face and costume.

World (fixed): Cao Wei in northern China, around 200–235 AD: the walled capitals of Xuchang, Ye and Luoyang, rammed-earth ramparts and tiled watchtowers, black-and-navy banners over vast northern plains, armoured cavalry, bronze ritual vessels and lacquered halls. Her costume, weapon and setting belong to this world.

Weapon (fixed — ours): a huge spiked war club.

Hair colour (fixed — ours): deep ink-blue hair. Keep exactly this hair colour; only the hairstyle is yours.

Skin tone (fixed — ours): light warm-beige skin with a golden undertone. Keep exactly this skin tone.

Costume colours (ours): deep navy blue, black lacquer, cold steel silver, ivory white.

Rank (fixed): she is a famed war general — her costume must read battlefield might at first glance: imposing, richly worked armour and cloth with flagship-card detail, never plain or sparse.

Exposure (fixed): bold — her outfit shows skin by design (a deep neckline, bare shoulders or arms, a high slit or short hem); intimate areas covered.

Face proportions: a short midface and a soft, gently rounded jawline with a small soft chin — never a long face or a long, pointed or heavy jaw; any crown or headpiece sits above her hairline and never lengthens her face. Her eyes stay at a natural open size — never squeezed into narrow slits.

Composition: vertical 2:3 full-body framing with modest headroom and clear space below the boots — the whole figure from the top of her crown or headpiece to both boots stays inside the frame, occupying about four-fifths of the image height, with the same camera distance in every genre; her hands and her signature item stay inside the frame. Camera at chest height with natural portrait perspective — no wide-angle distortion, no low angle, no close crop.

Costume silhouette chosen from our set: layered laced lamellar armor, big heavy beast-head pauldrons and armored skirts to the knees — a broad, weighty general's silhouette.

Original character and structural costume design: Her armor opens across the muscular upper chest and leaves her strong upper arms bare; a split ivory silk lower panel exposes one thigh. Interlocking crescent-shaped flank plates clamp across her ribs like a wrestler's braced embrace, a structural tribute to her legendary wrestling strength. A compact round face, bright amber eyes, thick straight brows, a tiny rounded nose, soft smiling lips. Ink-blue hair in a thick high braided ponytail with swept-back fringe. She stands squarely, both boots grounded, one hand holding her great iron spiked club vertically beside her, the other resting open at her waist. A broad Xuchang training court, rammed-earth wall and tiled gate behind her, bright morning.

She is strong and broad-shouldered with firm muscle, full bust, a defined waist, and rounded hips at natural human proportions. One head, two arms, two legs; both hands visible with five natural fingers each.

One figure only. No second person or creature. No logo, watermark, border, readable text or numbers. Three Kingdoms-era Chinese materials and setting only.

generation.summary: Round cheerful face, amber eyes; thick high braided ink-blue ponytail; heavy lamellar armor with broad beast-head shoulders and crescent flank braces; upright spiked club in a Han training court.
